title: Yagis, dishes and short antennas
blurb: Explain dish gain, how Yagi elements shape a beam, and why loading a short antenna lowers bandwidth and efficiency.

E9D01.why: Doubling frequency halves wavelength, so the dish doubles in wavelengths. Gain goes as that squared: ×4 = 10 log 4 = **6 dB**.
E9D01.trap: 3 dB is a doubling of power; here the gain quadruples.

E9D02.why: Two Yagis on **one axis, perpendicular**, driven elements at the same boom point and fed **90° out of phase** give a rotating field: circular polarization.
E9D02.trap: Stacking parallel Yagis only makes a more directional linear antenna.

E9D03.why: Current is highest low on the whip. A coil **near the center** keeps more current up the radiator than a base coil, so more of the antenna radiates.
E9D03.trap: Lower looks easier, but a base coil leaves less current up the radiator than a coil near the center.

E9D04.why: Coil resistance wastes power. A high reactance-to-resistance ratio (high Q) means little loss, so **efficiency** is maximized.
E9D04.trap: That is coil Q. High antenna Q is a different thing and narrows bandwidth.

E9D05.why: A Yagi's driven element is the resonant part fed by the line: about **½ wavelength**.

E9D06.why: A loading coil raises Q. Higher Q gives a sharper resonance, so the SWR bandwidth is **decreased**.
E9D06.trap: Coil position does not rescue bandwidth: any loading raises Q.

E9D07.why: A hat or wire at the top keeps current high along the radiator, which **improves radiation efficiency**.
E9D07.trap: Losses and Q do not improve; the benefit is radiation efficiency.

E9D08.why: Q measures how sharp the resonance is. Higher Q means a narrower band of good match: **SWR bandwidth decreases**.

E9D09.why: A short antenna has capacitive reactance. The coil adds equal inductive reactance, **cancelling** it so the antenna resonates.
E9D09.trap: The coil does not lower Q or losses; it raises Q and adds some loss.

E9D10.why: Below resonance the antenna is electrically shorter, and a shorter antenna has lower radiation resistance: it **decreases**.

E9D11.why: A reflector works with the driven element to put the energy forward, giving **higher gain** than a director in a two-element Yagi.

E9D12.why: Parasitic elements are excited by induction. Their length sets the **phase** of their current so radiation adds forward and cancels behind.
E9D12.trap: Mechanical balance has nothing to do with it.
